title: Hungarian B2
description: Dual-track B2 (Upper-Intermediate): a Core track mastering Hungarian information structure, advanced verbal derivation, participial syntax, modality, and rhetorical register through 36 adapted Hungarian literary classics, paired with a Culture, History & Society track ('Kultúra, történelem és társadalom') exploring Hungarian intellectual history, literary movements, scientific heritage, media, regional sociology, constitutional debates, and contemporary public life via 5-part serialized readings.
notes: STATUS (2026-09-25): Full 36-unit Dual-Track B2 Blueprint (36 Core units + 36 Culture, History & Society units = 72 units / 432 lessons total).
Each unit consists of 5 regular lessons plus 1 consolidation lesson (6 lessons/unit).

Core Track ('core'): Uses stem pattern b2-NN-01..b2-NN-05 + b2-NN-consolidation (e.g. b2-01-01..b2-01-consolidation). Each Core unit embeds ONE adapted Hungarian literary classic in Lesson 5 under content/hu/stories/classics/b2/b2-NN-<slug>.json.

Culture, History & Society Track ('culture'): Uses slug stem pattern b2-<slug>-01..b2-<slug>-05 + b2-<slug>-consolidation. Replicates the serialized world reading architecture: 5 per-lesson segments (content/hu/stories/world/b2/b2-<slug>-01-<seg>.json .. 05) embedded in Lessons 1-5 plus 1 combined standalone story (content/hu/stories/world/b2/b2-<slug>.json) for the Library.

Thematic & Grammatical Pairing: Every Track 2 unit is explicitly linked to its parallel Core B2 unit both thematically (applying the Core unit's communicative theme to a concrete Hungarian cultural, historical, or political phenomenon) and grammatically (teaching a complementary B2 grammatical structure tailored to narrating and analyzing that topic).

culture.title: Culture, History & Society
culture.description: Deep cultural, intellectual, historical, and political-sociological exploration of Hungary at B2 level. Each unit is directly paired with its corresponding Core B2 unit in topic and grammar, featuring a 5-part serialized world reading (stories/world/b2/b2-<slug>-01..05 + combined story).

units.title: The Coffeehouse Republic: Nyugat & Print Culture
units.hungarian: A kávéházi köztársaság: A Nyugat folyóirat és a sajtókultúra
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Budapest's 500 coffeehouses at the turn of the 20th century (New York, Centrál, Hadik), the founding of the journal Nyugat (1908), and the clash between modernist literary circles and conservative academicians.
units.grammar: Contrastive focus and topicalization (ami a konzervatívokat illeti...; ezzel szemben a Nyugat írói...) to contrast competing aesthetic and political camps
units.serializedStoryTitle: A New York kávéház tintatartója (5-part serialized history)

The Birth of Nyugat (1908)
Osvát Ernő, the Invisible Editor

units.title: Fin-de-Siècle Budapest & Hungarian Secession
units.hungarian: A századfordulós Budapest és a magyar szecesszió
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: How Budapest became Europe's fastest-growing metropolis (1873–1914): Ödön Lechner's quest for a Hungarian national architectural style, Zsolnay pyrogranite ceramics, and the transformation of avenues and tenements.
units.grammar: Extended pre-nominal participial modifiers (-ó/-ő and -t/-tt clauses before the noun: a Zsolnay-kerámiával díszített tetők) for architectural and urban description
units.serializedStoryTitle: Zsolnay-máz és vasbeton: Egy világváros születése
lessons: Uniting Buda, Pest, and Óbuda
Ödön Lechner and the Search for a National Style
Zsolnay Ceramics and Folk Motifs in Stone
Grand Boulevards and Courtyard Tenements
Reading History in Budapest's Facades

units.title: The Language Reform & the Politics of Hungarian
units.hungarian: A nyelvújítás és az anyanyelv politikája
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Ferenc Kazinczy and the 19th-century Nyelvújítás (Language Reform) that created ~10,000 new Hungarian words, the Orthologist vs. Neologist battle, and how Hungarian replaced Latin as the official language of state in 1844.
units.grammar: Action nominalizations (-ás/-és) and abstract noun derivations (-ság/-ség, -zat/-zet) mirroring how reformers engineered modern Hungarian vocabulary
units.serializedStoryTitle: Kazinczy tollától az államnyelvig

Kazinczy and the Neologist Revolution

units.title: The National Stage: Theatre, Censorship & Politics
units.hungarian: A nemzet színpada: Színház, cenzúra és politika
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Hungarian theatre as a substitute parliament under Habsburg and later authoritarian rule: from the opening of the Nemzeti Színház (1837) and Bánk bán on March 15, 1848, to the golden age of the Vígszínház and Hungarian operetta (Kálmán Imre, Lehár Ferenc).
units.grammar: Indirect commands, jussive clauses (-jon/-jen), and negative purpose clauses (nehogy a cenzor betiltsa...) describing theatrical subversion and staging

Budapest Operetta Conquerors the World
Director's Vision vs. State Censorship

units.title: Bartók, Kodály & the Ethnomusicological Revolution
units.hungarian: Bartók, Kodály és a népzenekutatás forradalma
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: How Béla Bartók and Zoltán Kodály traveled to remote villages with Edison phonograph cylinders to record ancient pentatonic folk songs, distinguishing authentic peasant music from urban 'magyar nóta' and creating modernist world music and the Kodály Method.
units.grammar: Frequentative/iterative verbs (-gat/-get, -dogál/-degél) and temporal/distributive structures describing fieldwork, recurring folk motifs, and musical transmission

units.title: Light, Myth & Modernism: Hungarian Visual Arts
units.hungarian: Fény, mítosz és modernség: A magyar képzőművészet
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: From Mihály Munkácsy's monumental realism and Pál Szinyei Merse's plein-air breakthrough (Majális) to the Nagybánya artists' colony, Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka's visionary canvases, and László Moholy-Nagy at the Bauhaus.

Art Museums, Collectors, and Cultural Memory

units.title: The 'Martians' of Budapest: Physics & Computing
units.hungarian: A budapesti 'marslakók': Fizika és számítástechnika
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Why a single generation from Budapest schools—János Neumann (von Neumann), Leó Szilárd, Jenő Wigner, Ede Teller, and Tódor Kármán—transformed nuclear physics, game theory, and modern computer architecture.
units.grammar: Proportional and conditional correlatives (amennyiben..., abban az esetben; minél összetettebb..., annál inkább...) explaining scientific theories and historical turning points
units.serializedStoryTitle: A marslakók már itt vannak: Neumann, Szilárd és a 20. század

units.title: Semmelweis, Szent-Györgyi & Medical Pioneers
units.hungarian: Semmelweis, Szent-Györgyi és az orvostudomány úttörői
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Ignác Semmelweis ('the Savior of Mothers') and institutional blindness in 19th-century Vienna and Pest, Albert Szent-Györgyi's discovery of Vitamin C in Szeged paprika, and Katalin Karikó's decades-long persistence with mRNA.
units.grammar: Past deontic and epistemic modals (megelőzhető lett volna, el kellett volna fogadniuk) analyzing institutional resistance and medical breakthroughs

lessons: Semmelweis and the Mystery of Childbed Fever
Why the Medical Establishment Refused to Listen
Szent-Györgyi Albert and the Szeged Laboratory
Katalin Karikó: Persistence Against Skepticism
Science, Ethics, and Public Trust

units.title: Non-Euclidean Worlds: Hungarian Mathematics & Chess
units.hungarian: Nemeuklideszi világok: A magyar matematika és sakkiskola
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: János Bolyai creating a new universe out of nothing in Transylvania, Paul Erdős's nomadic mathematical network ('My brain is open'), the KöMaL journal tradition, and the Polgár sisters redefining genius in chess.

units.title: The Fasori & Eötvös Tradition: Elite Education
units.hungarian: A Fasori gimnáziumtól az Eötvös Collegiumig: Oktatási örökség
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Inside the legendary secondary schools (Fasori Evangélikus Gimnázium, Minta Gimnázium, Piarista) and the Eötvös József Collegium: how teachers like László Rátz cultivated Nobel laureates, and modern debates over educational equity.

units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Sándor Ferenczi and the Budapest School of Psychoanalysis, its dialogue with writers like Kosztolányi, Csáth, and Babits, Michael Balint's doctor-patient groups, and Mihály Csíkszentmihályi's psychology of 'Flow'.

units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Hungarian industrial and everyday inventions: Farkas Kempelen's speaking machine, Ányos Jedlik's dynamo, the Ganz transformers, Donát Bánki's carburetor, László Bíró's ballpoint pen, Dénes Gábor's holography, and Ernő Rubik's three-dimensional spatial puzzle.

units.title: The Pesti Humor: Cabaret, Satire & Survival
units.hungarian: A pesti humor: Kabaré, szatíra és túlélés
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: How political cabaret (Endre Nagy, Béla Salamon, Géza Hofi) and satirical magazines (Borsszem Jankó, Ludas Matyi) used irony and double entendres as a survival mechanism through empire, war, and dictatorship.
units.grammar: Modal & pragmatic particles (hiszen, ugyebár, korántsem, aligha, éppenséggel) in ironic commentary and cabaret punchlines
units.serializedStoryTitle: Ha már sírni nem lehet: A pesti kabaré száz éve

units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: How cultural life operated under Kádár-era soft dictatorship via György Aczél's 'Three Ts' (Támogatott, Tűrt, Tiltott — Supported, Tolerated, Prohibited), self-censorship, and the underground Samizdat press (Beszélő, AB Kiadó) of the 1980s.

units.title: Great Intellectual Debates: Urbanists vs. Populists

units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: One of Hungary's defining 20th-century intellectual fault lines: the debate between the 'Népi' (Populist/Ruralist) movement focusing on the peasantry and folk roots (Illyés, Németh, Erdei) and the 'Urbánus' (Cosmopolitan/Urban) circle (Ignotus, Zsolt Béla, Fejtő) — and how it still echoes in public discourse.

units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: The evolution of Hungarian news and public information: Kossuth's Pesti Hírlap (1841), the golden age of feuilleton journalism, the Telephone Herald (Telefonhírmondó, 1893 — the world's first streaming news service), state television monopolies, and contemporary digital media polarization.

units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: The dramatic 20th- and 21st-century transformation of rural Hungary: traditional Alföld homesteads (tanyák), 1945 land distribution, forced collectivization vs. profitable 'household plots' (háztáji gazdaság), post-1990 rural depopulation, and modern eco-tourism and urban-to-rural migration.

units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Economic history of modern Hungary: the 1968 New Economic Mechanism (Új Gazdasági Mechanizmus), the shock of 1990s privatization and disappearance of heavy industry, foreign direct investment (automotive & tech hubs), inflation history (from the 1946 pengő to the forint), and economic convergence.

units.title: Central European Geopolitics & Visegrád Cooperation
units.hungarian: Közép-európai geopolitika és a visegrádi együttműködés
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: From the medieval 1335 Congress of Visegrád (Charles Robert, Casimir III, John of Bohemia) to the 1991 Visegrád Group (V4) revival, Hungary's strategic position between East and West, Danube macro-regional diplomacy, and debates over European sovereignty vs. federalization.
units.grammar: Diplomatic conditionals (indokolt volna, érdekükben állna) and abstract verbs governing sublative/allative (törekszik -ra, hozzájárul -hoz)
units.serializedStoryTitle: 1335-től a V4-ekig: Közép-Európa diplomáciája
lessons: 1335: Three Kings Meet at Visegrád Castle
1991: Rebuilding Central European Cooperation
Energy Routes, Trade Corridors, and Geography
Debates Over the Future Architecture of the European Union

units.title: Public Administration, Ombudsman & Civic Rights
units.hungarian: Közigazgatás, alapvető jogok biztosa és civil kurázsi
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Navigating high-register Hungarian institutional life: the Commissioner for Fundamental Rights (Alapvető Jogok Biztosa), constitutional complaints, administrative court procedures, consumer protection, freedom of information requests (közérdekű adatigénylés), and civic foundations.
units.grammar: Mastery of institutional verb-case government (hivatkozik -ra, fellebbez -ellen, eltekint -tól, kötelez -ra, beszámol -ról)
units.serializedStoryTitle: Hogyan érvényesítsük jogainkat? Közintézmények és polgárok

units.title: Paprika, Tokaj & Terroir: A Cultural History of Hungarian Cuisine
units.hungarian: Paprika, Tokaj és terroir: A magyar konyha kultúrtörténete
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: How Hungarian cuisine evolved over centuries: Renaissance court banquets under Matthias (onion, saffron, ginger), the Ottoman arrival of paprika and coffee, 19th-century French-Hungarian synthesis (Gundel Károly, Dobos C. József), Tokaj as the world's first classified wine region (1737), and the 21st-century Michelin gastronomic revolution.
units.grammar: Resultative sublatives (aranybarnára pirít, sűrűre főz) and hypothetical sensory comparisons (mintha + conditional)
units.serializedStoryTitle: Mátyás lakomájától a tokaji aszúig: Ízek és évszázadok
lessons: Before Paprika: Medieval and Renaissance Flavors
Tokaj-Hegyalja (1737): The World's First Classified Wine Region

The Modern Hungarian Culinary Renaissance

units.title: From Alfréd Hajós to the Aranycsapat: Sport & National Identity
units.hungarian: Hajós Alfrédtól az Aranycsapatig: Sport és nemzeti önkép
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Why Hungary ranks among the top 10 all-time Summer Olympic medal nations despite its size: Alfréd Hajós (Olympic swimming champion AND award-winning architect), the fencing and water polo dynasties, Puskás and the Golden Team's 6–3 triumph at Wembley (1953), and Krisztina Egerszegi & Katinka Hosszú.
units.grammar: Consecutive degree clauses (olyannyira..., hogy...) and dynamic preverb pairs (le-, meg-, túl-, végig-)
units.serializedStoryTitle: Hat-három és öt karika: A magyar sporttörténet legendái

units.title: Central European Political Thought: Széchenyi, Eötvös, Polányi, Bibó
units.hungarian: Közép-európai eszmetörténet: Széchenyi, Eötvös, Polányi és Bibó
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Four towering Hungarian thinkers on modernization, freedom, and society: István Széchenyi's gradualist civic reform (Hitel), József Eötvös's classic liberal treatise on nationalism and the state, Karl & Michael Polányi on market society and tacit knowledge, and István Bibó's diagnosis of Central European political hysteria.
units.grammar: Cleft-like identificational clauses (Az, ami...; abban rejlik, hogy...) and high-register academic synthesis
units.serializedStoryTitle: Szabadság és felelősség: Négy magyar gondolkodó

units.title: Beats, Festivals & Living Slang: Youth Culture Since the 1960s
units.hungarian: Beatkorszak, táncház és fesztiválok: Ifjúsági kultúra és élő nyelv
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: How each postwar Hungarian generation forged its own cultural space and language: the 1960s–70s Beat and Rock explosion (Illés, Omega, Locomotiv GT), the 1970s urban Táncház folk-revival subculture, 1980s underground art bands, the founding of Sziget Festival (1993), and how digital slang is reshaping spoken Hungarian today.
units.grammar: Expressive twin-words (ikerítő szavak), colloquial ellipsis, and register shifting between informal youth speech and standard prose

units.title: Hungary in the 21st-Century Knowledge Economy
units.hungarian: Magyarország a 21. századi tudásalapú gazdaságban
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Contemporary science and technology in Hungary: the ELI-ALPS laser research center in Szeged (Gérard Mourou & Ferenc Krausz, 2023 Nobel Prize in Attosecond Physics), biotechnology, autonomous vehicle engineering, renewable energy transition, and ethical debates around AI for medium-sized languages.
units.grammar: Speculative & counterfactual multi-clause conditionals (amennyiben... válna; ha ...-na/-ne, akkor sem ...-hatna/-hetne)

units.title: Synthesis: What It Means to Speak and Understand Hungarian Today
units.hungarian: Szintézis: Mit jelent ma magyarul érteni és gondolkodni?
units.culturalHistoricalPoliticalTopic: Capstone reflection on the Hungarian cultural universe: how an isolated Finno-Ugric language in the heart of Europe absorbed Turkic, Slavic, Latin, German, and modern global influences while keeping its unmistakable logic, humor, poetic density, and historical self-awareness.
